_about: Every QTT OS app screen the assistant may point to. id = what the app opens; product = null for the app itself. roles: '*' = anyone with that app; product roles by name; '@owner' = business owner/admin; '@manager' = has people reporting to them. tips: shown on that screen (and used by the assistant); 'when' names a condition in qtt_platform.assistant.conditions.

shift_types.name: Fixed work week
shift_types.how: Make the shift, then a shift pattern that repeats every week.

shift_types.name: A different place on some days
shift_types.how: In the pattern, choose office, from home or anywhere for each day.

shift_types.name: Field work
shift_types.example: A sales rep checks in from anywhere
shift_types.how: Choose Anywhere as the place — no office area is checked.

shift_types.name: Week rotation (2–4 weeks)
shift_types.example: Week A days, week B nights
shift_types.how: A pattern that repeats every 2, 3 or 4 weeks.

shift_types.name: Long week rotation (up to 8 weeks)
shift_types.how: A pattern that repeats every 5 to 8 weeks.

shift_types.name: Day-cycle rotation
shift_types.example: 4 on / 4 off; 2-2-3; four crews over 28 days
shift_types.how: A pattern that repeats every N days (2 to 56), whatever the weekday.

shift_types.name: Night shift past midnight
shift_types.how: End the shift earlier than it starts. The check-out counts for the day the shift started.

shift_types.name: Night shift, then a morning shift
shift_types.example: Night on Monday, morning on Wednesday
shift_types.how: Works as it is — each check-in and check-out goes to the right day.

shift_types.name: 24-hour duty with a day off after
shift_types.how: A 24-hour shift (start and end at the same time) in a pattern with a day off after each duty.

shift_types.name: Back-to-back 24-hour duties
shift_types.how: Not supported: leave a day off between duties, or use two 12-hour shifts.

shift_types.name: Work at a site
shift_types.example: Guard at Gate A, nurse in Ward 3
shift_types.how: Add the site with its check-in area; choose it for a day in the pattern.

shift_types.name: One-day change
shift_types.example: Ravi on nights only on 20 Oct, or a day off
shift_types.how: People › the person › Shifts. Editing the pattern later keeps it.

shift_types.name: Breaks
shift_types.how: Set the break on the shift; unpaid breaks are taken off the hours worked.

shift_types.name: Split shift
shift_types.how: One shift with time off in the middle.

shift_types.name: Shift change and swap by request
shift_types.how: People ask in My requests; approvers decide.

shift_types.name: Overtime paid in payroll
shift_types.how: Approved overtime goes into the next payroll run.

shift_types.name: Minimum staff, handover, on-call
shift_types.example: At least 2 guards on Gate A nights
shift_types.how: Coverage rules, handover notes and the on-call roster.

shift_types.name: Sites without network
shift_types.example: A check-in at a remote site
shift_types.how: The check-in is saved on the phone and sent later.

shift_types.name: Two different shifts in one day
shift_types.example: Morning at site A, evening at site B
shift_types.how: Not supported: use a split shift if both parts are at the same place.

shift_types.name: Flexi hours
shift_types.how: Not supported: use one long shift with late marking off.

screens.title: Home
screens.what: Your apps, the For you cards (what needs you now) and search across everything.

screens.title: Search
screens.what: One search for customers, people, items and apps. Understands typos, any word order and phone numbers.

screens.title: Customers
screens.what: One customer list shared by every app (Onbox chats, Orbitra bills). Add, tag, archive; call, WhatsApp or email a customer.

screens.title: Add customer
screens.what: Add an individual or a business (GSTIN, billing address, tags).

screens.title: Business profile
screens.what: Logo, address, GSTIN, contact details, bank and UPI — used on invoices, payslips and PDFs. Only the owner or an admin can change them.

screens.title: Team
screens.what: Invite teammates by email, choose which apps each person can use and their role in each app, remove people.

screens.title: Plans
screens.what: Each app's plan and trial end date. To upgrade or change a plan, contact Queen Touch Technology.

screens.title: Account
screens.what: Your accounts (switch between several), appearance, language, tips, help and support, fingerprint / Face ID sign-in, sign out.

screens.title: Appearance
screens.what: Light, dark or system mode, theme, text size and density.

screens.title: Office Pulse
screens.what: Check in / out, today's team (managers, HR), your tiles: attendance, leave, expenses, payslips.

screens.title: My attendance
screens.what: Your month calendar: in / out times, hours, late days. Request Work From Home or On Duty for past or coming days (a manager or HR approves).

tips.text: Working from home or out on work? Request Work From Home or On Duty here — your manager approves it.
tips.label: Request work from home

screens.title: Leave
screens.what: Your leave balances, apply for leave (half days allowed; holidays not counted), your requests; withdraw open or future ones.

tips.text: Working from home instead of taking leave? Ask for Work From Home — it doesn't use your leave balance.
tips.label: Request work from home

tips.text: Your business allows checking in away from the office: just add a reason when you check in.
tips.label: Check in

screens.title: Expenses
screens.what: Your expense claims and their status; new claim with several expenses and receipt photos; withdraw a pending claim.

tips.text: Add a photo of each receipt — claims with receipts are approved faster.
tips.label: New expense claim

screens.title: New expense claim
screens.path: Office Pulse › Expenses › New expense claim
screens.what: One claim: what for, amount and date per expense, details, receipt photos (up to 5 MB each).

screens.title: Payslips
screens.what: Your payslips, newest first: earnings, deductions, net pay; download the PDF. They appear after HR runs and finalises payroll.

screens.title: Team today
screens.what: Who is in, out, on leave or not in yet today (remote check-ins are marked).

screens.title: Approvals
screens.what: Requests waiting at a step you approve — leave, work from home / on duty, expenses, late check-ins, missed check-outs, shift changes and swaps, early exits, overtime. Filter pills by kind; leave cards show the balance left and, with Coverage, a warning when approving would leave a shift short. A swap partner sees Accept / Decline first.

screens.title: People
screens.what: Employees (working / left): add, edit, give app access (email invitation), mark attendance, salary, mark as left. On top: action cards — import the team from Excel, invite everyone with an email in one tap, download people missing a mobile or department to fix them in Excel — and Import / Export (Excel or CSV) buttons.

screens.title: Import employees
screens.what: Import employees from Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (up to 1,000): a template to download; columns recognised by name (also misspelt, else suggested by QTT Assistant) and changeable; each row checked — new, update (matched by employee ID, email or mobile) or a problem with the reason; suggestions (new departments, missing mobiles, plan room); optional app invitations; large files continue in the background. QTT can import it for you.

guide.intro: Bring many people in at once from an Excel or CSV file — or update people already here. Nothing is saved until you've seen what will happen.
steps: Tap Download the template, or use your own list: columns like Name, DOJ, Phone or Designation are recognised.
Fill in one person per row. Someone new needs a name, gender and date of birth; dates are day/month/year.
Tap Choose file. You see who is new, who will be updated (matched by Employee ID, email or mobile) and any problems.
Check the columns: change any that were recognised wrongly. Rows with problems are skipped — fix them in the file and import again.
Switch on Invite new people with an email if they should get the app, then tap Import.
To fix details later: People › Export, edit the file, and import it back — the Employee ID column matches each person.

suggestions.text: Start with 2–3 people to see how it works, then import the rest.
Big list or a messy file? Send it to QTT from this screen and we'll import it for you.

screens.title: Setup
screens.what: Check-in rules (ask for location; allow check-in away from the office), offices and their check-in radius, business type and capabilities, sites, shifts (hours, late after, break, split), shift patterns, approval flows, attendance rules, leave types and giving leave, holiday calendars, departments and job titles.

tips.text: Turn on “Allow check-in away from the office” so people can work from home and check in with a reason.
tips.label: Open Setup

screens.title: Payroll
screens.what: Steps: 1) a salary template with pay items (formulas allowed, e.g. base * 0.4), 2) give it to people with their monthly salary, 3) run payroll for a month, check, then finalise and publish payslips.

screens.title: Business type
screens.path: Office Pulse › Manage › Setup › Business type
screens.what: Pick the kind of business (office, security, hospital, factory, retail). Its preset switches on the capabilities it usually needs — Flexible cycles, Sites, Requests, Split shifts, Overtime pay, Coverage (with handover and on-call), Offline attendance — and suggested attendance rules. Everything can be changed afterwards.

guide.intro: Tell Office Pulse what kind of business you run. It switches on the features that kind of business usually needs and suggests attendance rules. You can change any of it later.
steps: Choose your business type.
Tap Use to switch on its features and suggested rules — or switch features on and off one by one below.
Then check Attendance rules and Shift patterns: the preset is only a starting point.

suggestions.text: Offices need nothing extra: a work-week shift pattern, late check-in approval and check-out reminders are enough.
Turn on Sites (each client site or gate), Flexible cycles (4 on / 4 off, 12-hour shifts), Coverage (guards per gate) and Offline attendance for sites with weak network.
Use Flexible cycles for a 28-day rotation, wards as Sites, Coverage rules per ward and handover notes between shifts.
Use a week rotation for A / B / C shifts, Requests for overtime approval and Overtime pay so approved hours reach payroll.
Make each store a Site, use Split shifts for the lunch and dinner rush, and let staff swap shifts by request.
Not sure? Start with Office and switch a feature on when you need it.

screens.title: Shifts
screens.what: Working hours: start, end (an end before the start means the next day), late after minutes, automatic attendance, a break rule (unpaid minutes after hours worked, or paid), and — with Split shifts — time off in the middle.

guide.intro: A shift is a set of working hours. Make your shifts first; shift patterns then say who works which shift on which day.
steps: Tap New shift: give it a name, a start and an end. An end earlier than the start (22:00 → 06:00) means it ends the next morning.
Late after: how many minutes after the start a check-in counts as late.
Break: how many minutes, and after how many hours of work. An unpaid break is taken off the hours worked — unless they checked out for it.
Split shift (needs Split shifts): the time off in the middle, e.g. off 15:00, back 18:00. That time never counts as work, and checking out for it isn't an early exit.
Give the shift to people with Shift patterns.

suggestions.text: Most businesses: a 30-minute unpaid break after 6 hours.
Restaurants: one split shift 11:00–22:00, off 15:00–18:00.
12-hour day and night shifts (08:00–20:00 and 20:00–08:00) with a 60-minute break after 6 hours.
Morning 07:00–15:00, evening 15:00–23:00 and night 23:00–07:00, each with a 30-minute break.
Three 8-hour shifts — A 06:00–14:00, B 14:00–22:00, C 22:00–06:00 — with late after 5 minutes.

screens.title: Shift patterns
screens.path: Office Pulse › Manage › Setup › Shift patterns
screens.what: Which shift on which day, and where (office, from home, anywhere or a site): the same every week, a rotation of up to 8 weeks, or (Flexible cycles) every N days like 4 on / 4 off. Applies to everyone, a department or chosen people; gives shifts 60 days ahead. One-day changes in People are kept.

guide.intro: A shift pattern gives people their shifts automatically — which shift on which day, and where. Save it once; Office Pulse gives shifts 60 days ahead and keeps adding more.
steps: Make your shifts first in Setup › Shifts.
Tap New shift pattern: a name and the first day (a Monday for a weekly pattern).
Choose how it repeats: every week, every 2 to 8 weeks for a rotation, or every few days like 4 on / 4 off (needs Flexible cycles).
Tap each day: pick the shift and where — at the office, from home, anywhere or at a site. Leave a day off.
Choose who: everyone, a department or chosen people. Chosen people come first, then a department, then everyone.
Save and apply. You get a notification when everyone has their shifts. For one day only, change it in People › the person › Shifts — editing the pattern later keeps that change.

suggestions.text: Office week: Monday to Friday at the office, Saturday half day from home, Sunday off.
4 on / 4 off: repeat every 8 days, days 1–4 the 12-hour shift at the client site.
Four crews: repeat every 28 days — 7 days, 7 off, 7 nights, 7 off — one pattern per crew with a different start day.
Three-week rotation: week 1 shift A, week 2 shift B, week 3 shift C.
One weekly pattern per store, with the split shift on the busy days.
Night shifts that end after midnight work as they are: the check-out counts for the day the shift started.

screens.title: Attendance rules
screens.path: Office Pulse › Manage › Setup › Attendance rules
screens.what: Late check-ins needing approval (after N minutes; if not approved: half day, absent or late mark), check-out required with reminders and what happens without one, how long a forgotten check-out stays open, early exits and overtime needing approval, how long offline check-ins are accepted, and the morning coverage alert.

guide.intro: Your own rules for late arrivals, forgotten check-outs, leaving early and overtime. Every business chooses differently.
steps: Late check-ins: switch on Late check-ins need approval, choose after how many minutes, and what the day becomes if it's not approved.
Check-out: switch on Check-out required. People get a reminder when the shift ends; choose what happens if they still don't check out.
Forgotten check-out: how many hours after the shift a check-out still counts. Night shifts need about 12.
Early exit and overtime (needs Requests): leaving well before the end, or staying well after it, goes to the approver.
Offline and coverage: how long check-ins saved on a phone can be sent later, and whether HR hears about coverage gaps each morning.

suggestions.text: Late after 15 minutes, half day if not approved; check-out required with a 30-minute reminder.
Late after 10 minutes with a late mark only; keep a forgotten check-out open for 6 hours.
Late after 10 minutes; keep a forgotten check-out open for 12 hours for night shifts.
Late after 5 minutes, half day if not approved; overtime after 15 minutes needs approval.
Late after 10 minutes; early exits after 10 minutes need approval.

screens.title: My requests
screens.what: Your shift changes, shift swaps, early exits, overtime, late check-ins and missed check-outs, with who each is waiting for. New request (when the business uses Requests): another shift / place / day off, a swap with a colleague (they accept first), leaving early, or overtime.

guide.intro: Ask for a different shift, swap with a colleague, leave early or work overtime. Each request goes to the people who approve it.
steps: Tap New request and choose what you need.
Shift change: the day, then another shift and place — or the day off.
Shift swap: your day, the colleague, and their day (empty = swap shifts on the same day). They accept first, then it goes for approval.
Early exit or overtime: the day and the time or minutes.
Follow it here: you see the status and who it's waiting for.

suggestions.text: Ask at least a day before, so your manager can arrange cover.

screens.title: Approval flows
screens.path: Office Pulse › Manage › Setup › Approval flows
screens.what: Per kind of request (leave, work from home, expense, late check-in, missed check-out, shift change, swap, early exit, overtime): up to 5 steps — manager, manager's manager, HR, HR Admin or a chosen person — each optionally only above an amount, days or minutes, with HR added after N hours waiting. No steps: the manager or HR.

guide.intro: Decide who approves each kind of request, step by step. Without steps, the person's manager — or HR — approves.
steps: Open a kind of request: Leave, Expense, Overtime and so on.
Add steps in order: the manager, the manager's manager, HR, HR Admin or a chosen person.
A step can apply only above an amount, a number of days or minutes — for example, leave over 3 days also goes to HR.
Add HR after (hours): if a step waits too long, HR can decide it too.
A rejection at any step ends the request; the last approval applies it.

suggestions.text: Leave: the manager; above 3 days, then HR. Expense: the manager; above ₹5,000, then HR Admin.
Overtime: the manager, then HR above 120 minutes.
Shift swap: the supervisor (manager) only, with HR added after 12 hours.

screens.title: Overtime and on-call pay
screens.path: Office Pulse › Manage › Payroll › Overtime and on-call pay
screens.what: How approved overtime and on-call days are paid in payroll runs (Overtime pay capability): hourly rate (monthly base ÷ days ÷ hours, or a fixed rate), multiplier, counting in blocks of minutes, on-call allowance per day. Each is paid once; HR sees what's added before slips are made.

guide.intro: Approved overtime and on-call days are added to the next payroll run, as their own pay items. Each is paid only once.
steps: Hourly rate: the monthly salary ÷ days in a month ÷ hours in a day — or set a fixed rate per hour.
Multiplier: 1.5 pays time and a half, 2 pays double.
Blocks: overtime is counted in whole blocks, e.g. 15 minutes — 50 minutes counts as 45.
On-call allowance: an amount per day on call (0 = not paid).
Run payroll as usual: before the slips are made you see the overtime and on-call it will add.

suggestions.text: Factories usually pay overtime at double the ordinary rate — check your state's labour rules.
Only people with a salary set are paid; give everyone their salary in Payroll first.

screens.title: Coverage
screens.what: Coverage capability: rules for the fewest people a shift (at a site, on chosen weekdays) needs; the next 2 weeks with gaps; a 07:00 alert to HR for the next 3 days; warnings on approvals when leave or a shift change would leave a shift short. Handover notes from the end of a shift show on the next shift's check-in card.

guide.intro: Make sure every shift has enough people. Add a rule and Office Pulse shows the gaps for the next 2 weeks — before they happen.
steps: Tap Add a rule: the shift, the site (optional), at least how many people, and the days (none = every day).
Check Gaps: a red number means people are missing that day. Fix it with a one-day change in People or with a shift pattern.
Every morning at 7, HR gets the gaps for the next 3 days (switch it off in Attendance rules).
When someone asks for leave or a shift change that would leave a shift short, the approver sees a warning on the request.
Handover: at the end of a shift, people tap Leave a handover note on their check-in card; the next shift sees it when they open the app.

suggestions.text: Gate A nights: at least 2 guards, every day.
Ward 3 nights: at least 3 nurses, every day.
Weekend evenings: at least 4 on the evening shift, Saturday and Sunday.
Each line: at least 6 people on every shift.

screens.title: On call
screens.what: Coverage capability: who is on call now and next; add one person for some days, or a rotation where chosen people take turns (days each, times round). On call now shows on Team today and the person's check-in card; paid per day when HR Admin sets an on-call allowance.

guide.intro: Who answers out of hours. Add one person for some days, or a rotation where people take turns.
steps: Add on call: choose the person and the days.
Rotation: tick the people in the order they take turns, how many days each, and how many times round the list.
On call now shows on Team today and on that person's check-in card.
To pay it, HR Admin sets an on-call allowance per day in Payroll › Overtime and on-call pay.

suggestions.text: A weekly rotation: 7 days each, 4 times round — about a month planned at once.

screens.title: Orbitra
screens.what: Today's sales, money to collect, items running low, and your tiles.

screens.title: POS
screens.what: Quick counter sale: tap items (search or barcode), choose a customer or walk-in, take payment (cash, UPI, card, or split; change is worked out), save the bill PDF.

screens.title: Sales
screens.what: Invoices (unpaid first) and quotes: new invoice, new quote, receive a payment, save or share the PDF, take back items (credit note), turn a quote into an invoice.

tips.text: Send prices first with a quote; turn it into an invoice when they agree.
tips.label: New invoice

screens.title: New invoice
screens.what: Bill a customer: items, GST, total, paid now or later.

screens.title: Inventory
screens.what: Items and services: price, cost, GST rate, HSN/SAC, barcode, low-stock level; add stock, count stock, move between stores; running-low list.

tips.text: Set “Tell me when stock is at or below” on an item and Orbitra warns you before it runs out.
tips.label: Open Inventory

screens.title: Purchases
screens.what: Supplier bills (stock comes in), what you still owe, suppliers, pay a supplier. Needs a plan with Purchases.

screens.title: Orbitra customers
screens.what: Who owes you and what they bought; new invoice or receive payment for a customer.

screens.title: Accounts
screens.what: Money in and out, record shop expenses (rent, electricity…), move money between cash and bank, who owes you and whom you owe. Needs a plan with Accounts.

screens.title: Reports
screens.what: For a period: sales by day, best sellers, best customers, GST (collected minus paid on purchases), profit, stock value. Needs a plan with Reports.

screens.title: Orbitra settings
screens.what: Selling prices include GST (on/off), main store, invoice note, run setup again. Business details on invoices come from Business › Profile.

screens.title: Onbox
screens.what: All your channels with open and unread counts; tap one to see its conversations.

screens.title: Conversations
screens.what: Customer chats from WhatsApp, website chat, Facebook, Instagram and email: Mine / Unassigned / All, filter by status and channel, reply or add private notes, assign, snooze, label, resolve, save the contact as a customer. WhatsApp replies are free-form only within 24 hours of the customer's last message.

screens.title: Onbox settings
screens.what: Channels: connect WhatsApp (Meta Cloud API), website chat (paste the code on your site), Facebook, Instagram, email (forwarding or mailbox); rename or remove. Channel access: choose which team members answer each channel (managers and supervisors see all).

screens.title: Managed Services
screens.what: Everything QTT runs for you: status of your websites and systems, your services, previews to approve, connecting your domain to go live, recent activity.

screens.title: All services
screens.what: Every service QTT offers with its price; suggestions for your kind of business; start a free one instantly or pay to start (the owner orders).

screens.title: Requests
screens.what: Ask QTT for a change or help; mark it urgent if something is broken; QTT replies there.

screens.title: Payments
screens.what: Your invoices for services and paying them (UPI, card or net banking).
